text:
oncall-bot: Pager: continuous-batch error-rate spike detected in prod-west - metric: batch_fail_rate +420% over baseline, KV cache evictions +12x, latency p95 up 3x. Priority: P1.

mei: taking it. seeing a large tail of requests flagged as function_invoke with structured JSON-array outputs. likely causing KV key explosion + batch fragmentation. investigating source.

sam: noted. can you paste an example payload pattern? this sounds like the structured-output length variance we saw in staging.

mei: example snippet from logs (sanitized):
```
{"request_id":"r-9a1","route":"/gen","meta":{"has_function":true,"structured_output":true},"output":[{"tool":"search","resp":"..."},{"tool":"format","resp":"[...large array...]"}]}
```
These end up generating unique cache prefixes per element, KC size balloons. continuous batching tries to pack them but fragmentation causes tiny batches and many uncacheable prefixes.

jordan: sounds like the same regression as last month but with structured arrays instead of nested objects. runbook step A: disable continuous batching for requests with meta.has_function=true. we can do a scoped config toggle.

olivia: customer impact so far? I see traces showing 502 spikes for some routes.

mei: quick summary: ~7 customers saw increased 5xx/timeouts over the past 8m. one high-volume tenant saw 502s for ~4m. error budget burn noted but not full SLA breach yet. attaching links to traces in console (link omitted).

sam: ok. propose emergency hotfix: patch runtime config to set runtime.continuous_batching.enabled=false for selector "meta.has_function==true || meta.structured_output==true"; also throttle KV prefetch: kv_cache.prefetch.enabled=false for the same selector. both changes should reduce cache churn and let batching fall back to per-request handling.

mei: I'm going to apply the scoped change now. If anyone objects speak up.

sre-deploy-bot: redwood-config apply --env=prod --patch - <<PATCH
selector: meta.has_function==true || meta.structured_output==true
patch:
  runtime:
    continuous_batching:
      enabled: false
  kv_cache:
    prefetch:
      enabled: false
PATCH

sre-deploy-bot: Patch accepted. Rolling update on runtime pool prod-west nodes (n=12).

jordan: also pushing a short-term increase to kv_cache.max_entries to absorb current thrash until we re-evaluate prefetch strategy: setting kv_cache.max_entries=750000 for prod-west.

sre-deploy-bot: Config change committed: kv_cache.max_entries=750000. Rolling config apply.

mei: after the patch p95 latency dropped ~35% within 90s, cache eviction rate down to near-baseline, error rate trending back down. I'm leaving a trace in #incidents-postmortems and tagging runtime for follow-up.

olivia: escalating to account teams: sending a short incident note to affected customers with current status and mitigation steps.

sam: assigning a follow-up: root cause: structured-array outputs cause high-entropy cache prefixes + batch scheduler misestimation. follow-ups: (1) add guard to batching to detect variable-length structured arrays and avoid grouping them; (2) improve cache key normalization for tool outputs; (3) evaluate selective prefetch heuristics. I'll own 1 and 2, mei will defer 3 to infra.

jordan: we'll prepare a fast rollout of a smarter batching heuristic ( cap per-request batch-size when meta.structured_output==true ) as a staged change.

mei: closing pager for now — system stabilized. please join post-incident call at 16:30 to capture actionable items. :white_check_mark: 

oncall-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED by mei. Duration: 00:25:58.

mei: postmortem owner: sam. timeline + logs are in the incident doc. assigning follow-ups in Jira (links omitted). Thanks all for quick responses. :raised_hands:
